hero.title: IRATA Level 1 — Rope Access Technician
hero.body: The formal entry point into the rope access industry. Six days building rope manoeuvres, equipment inspection, and basic rescue — closing with an independent IRATA assessment.

card.summary: The formal entry point into the rope access industry. Six days building rope manoeuvres, equipment inspection, and basic rescue — closing with an independent IRATA assessment.

course.summary: The formal entry point into the rope access industry. Six days building rope manoeuvres, equipment inspection, and basic rescue — closing with an independent IRATA assessment.
prerequisites: Medically fit for work at height, supported by a doctor’s statement
No history of vertigo, epilepsy, or uncontrolled cardiac conditions
No prior rope access experience required
outcomes: Ascend, descend, and change ropes on two independent points of attachment
Negotiate deviations, rope-to-rope transfers, knots, and edge transitions
Inspect and document the serviceability of PPE and hardware
Perform a straightforward casualty rescue from a descent
Apply the hierarchy of control and the IRATA ICOP safe system of work

syllabus.title: Day 1 — Foundations & Equipment
syllabus.detail: Regulatory framework, the IRATA ICOP, anatomy of a twin-rope system, familiarisation and pre-use inspection of all PPE, core working knots.

syllabus.title: Day 2 — Core Manoeuvres
syllabus.detail: Controlled ascent and descent, changeovers, small deviations, and managing the working line under load.

syllabus.title: Day 3 — Advanced Manoeuvres
syllabus.detail: Rope-to-rope transfers, passing mid-line knots, edge transitions, and working from re-anchors.

syllabus.title: Day 4 — Rescue
syllabus.detail: Descent rescues, rescues from ascent, use of dedicated rescue devices, and realistic scenario simulations.

syllabus.title: Day 5 — Consolidation
syllabus.detail: Integrated scenario practice, logbook documentation review, and an internal mock assessment.

syllabus.title: Day 6 — IRATA Assessment
syllabus.detail: Assessment by an independent IRATA Assessor: written theory, equipment inspection, manoeuvres, and rescue.

course.certificate: IRATA Level 1 card and certificate, valid for 3 years, registered in the IRATA International database.

sections.body:
## Who this course is for

Level 1 is designed for technicians who have never worked on rope, and for ground-based specialists — welders, inspectors, mechanical fitters, industrial photographers — who need to reach work areas that scaffolding cannot serve.

On passing, you may work under the direct supervision of an IRATA Level 3 on any site operating to the IRATA scheme.

## How we teach

We hold our instructor-to-trainee ratio at a maximum of 1:6, well below the IRATA ceiling. Every manoeuvre you make is watched, corrected, and repeated until it is right — not demonstrated once at the front of the room.

All PPE is supplied by RAC and re-inspected each morning. Trainees need only bring safety boots and work clothing.
